Chapter 9. Transformation and Growth: Words as Seeds.
Change almost never happens overnight, does it? More often, it’s this slow, gentle unfolding—a gradual shift that’s hard to notice until one day, you look back and realize everything feels different.
Think about how powerful words can be. Prayer and poetry, for example, are like seeds of transformation. They nurture growth in such subtle, almost invisible ways—but their impact can be absolutely profound.
Picture someone who’s always struggled with self-doubt. Maybe for years, they’ve carried this heavy feeling of not being enough, of always falling short. Then, out of the blue, they stumble upon a poem about resilience—about the courage to start again, no matter what. Those words stick with them. They echo in the back of their mind, quietly becoming a mantra. A soft reminder to be gentle, to treat themselves with kindness. And while the change isn’t instant, over time, those old patterns start to loosen their grip.
Prayer works in a similar way. Say you’re at a crossroads, not sure which path to take, so you pray for guidance. The answer doesn’t show up as a lightning bolt. Instead, it might arrive in tiny nudges—a heartfelt conversation with a friend, a moment of clarity during a quiet walk, or maybe even a line from a poem that feels like it’s meant just for you. When you look back, you realize your prayer was answered, just not in the way you expected.
Most of us don’t realize just how much words shape how we see ourselves, and the world around us. Imagine a teacher sharing a poem with a class. Suddenly, a student who’s always felt invisible feels seen—maybe for the very first time. Or think of a community coming together to pray for justice. Just speaking those words aloud, together, sparks a sense of purpose—a commitment to take action, to make a difference.
Over time, the seeds that prayer and poetry plant start to take root. The changes might seem small at first—maybe a little more patience, a little more hope—but they add up. Those words become part of your story, woven right into the fabric of your everyday life.
Real transformation isn’t usually dramatic. It’s found in those quiet moments—the willingness to keep showing up, to keep speaking, to keep listening, to keep hoping. Prayer and poetry both give us a way to nurture that kind of growth. They help us believe that change is possible, even when it’s hard to see.
